NDT training in Kansas City: how it works for Kansas City employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training for Kansas City employers and technicians on both sides of the state line, delivered live online or onsite at your facility in Missouri or Kansas. We deliver the classroom training; your employer's written practice governs experience, exams and certification, with an ASNT Level III administering the examinations. Level I and II courses cover UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III preparation.

Kansas City is a crossroads market. It sits at the junction of several Class I railroads, on major pipeline and refined-product corridors, within reach of two nuclear generating stations, and at the centre of a regional manufacturing economy that runs from auto assembly to precision defence work. It is also home to two of the country's largest engineering and construction firms in the power, utility and infrastructure space. That combination means NDT technicians here work on everything from rail tank cars and bridges to power plant outages and pipeline construction.

One detail makes Kansas City unusual: it straddles two regulatory regimes for radiography, because Kansas is an NRC Agreement State and Missouri is not. We explain what that means for RT crews below.

Atlantis has no physical training centre in Kansas City. We bring the training to your people through live-virtual classrooms and onsite sessions at your shop, plant or yard, under ASNT Level III oversight. Request a Kansas City training quote and we will reply within one business day.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Kansas City

Courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A and the ANSI/ASNT CP-105 topical outlines, covering principles, equipment, calibration, technique, interpretation against codes and reporting. Level III preparation adds method depth and the basic examination. Here is how each method maps to Kansas City work.

MethodLevelsWhat Kansas City employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, III prepRail wheel, axle and rail weld inspection; bridge and structural welds to AWS D1.5 and D1.1; thickness surveys on terminal tanks and plant pipingLevel I: employer entry requirements. Level II: Level I plus documented experience
Phased Array UT (PAUT)I, IIPipeline and plant piping welds, pressure equipment, power plant components during outagesConventional UT Level II strongly recommended
Time-of-Flight Diffraction (TOFD)I, IIFlaw sizing on thick-wall welds in power and pressure equipment fabricationConventional UT Level II strongly recommended
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, III prepPipeline girth welds to API 1104, piping to ASME B31.1 and B31.3, pressure vessel welds, castingsRadiation safety training and certification per NRC or Kansas rules before handling sources
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, II, III prepRail car and locomotive components, welded structures, bridge steel, forgings and heavy equipmentEmployer entry requirements
Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, II, III prepPrecision components, stainless piping, non-magnetic castings, aviation componentsEmployer entry requirements
Visual Testing (VT)I, II, III prepWeld inspection across fabrication, rail car repair and bridge work; outage inspectionsEmployer entry requirements
Eddy Current Testing (ET)I, IIHeat exchanger and condenser tubing at power stations, surface crack detection on componentsEmployer entry requirements

Kansas City contractors who work power outages usually want UT, ET and PAUT; rail shops lean on MT, UT and VT; pipeline crews prioritise RT and increasingly PAUT. Book a Level III consultation if you want help sequencing methods for your business.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Kansas City, step by step

Neither Missouri nor Kansas issues an NDT technician licence, and under SNT-TC-1A certification is granted by the employer, not ASNT. The path:

  1. Employer written practice describing training, examination and certification for each method and level. See written practice development.
  2. Classroom training for the hours your written practice requires, delivered by Atlantis online or onsite. Check recommended hours in the training requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience, documented, under qualified supervision.
  4. General examination on the principles of the method.
  5. Specific examination on your employer's equipment, procedures, codes and specifications.
  6. Practical examination on real specimens, graded by a Level III or designated examiner.
  7. Vision examination, repeated at least annually.
  8. Certification by the employer after Level III review.
  9. Recertification at the interval in the written practice.

More detail: SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Kansas City crews

Kansas City employers often run crews across a wide region, from Wichita and Topeka to Springfield, St. Louis and Omaha. Pulling everyone into one place is expensive. Atlantis offers:

  • Live online classroom for theory and Level III preparation, reachable from wherever the crew is based. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility in the metro or the surrounding region, using your equipment, specimens and procedures, under ASNT Level III oversight.
  • Blended, theory online, practicals and exams onsite.

We schedule around spring and fall power plant outages, pipeline construction seasons and your own production cycles. Ask about onsite training for your Kansas City crew; quotes within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Kansas City

Rail

Kansas City is one of the largest rail hubs in the US, served by several Class I railroads and home to major yards, terminals and car repair shops. Rail NDT covers wheels, axles, bearings, couplers, rail welds, tank cars and bridges. Work on tank cars and freight cars is shaped by Association of American Railroads standards and Federal Railroad Administration rules, and rail operators run their own qualification programmes on top of SNT-TC-1A-style training. MT, UT and VT are the core methods.

Power generation and engineering

Two nuclear generating stations lie within a few hours' drive, Wolf Creek in Kansas and Callaway in Missouri, along with coal and gas stations across both states. Outages bring ET on condensers and heat exchangers, UT and PAUT on piping and components, and MT/PT on rotating equipment. Nuclear in-service inspection follows ASME Section XI and the operator's qualification requirements, which typically exceed a basic SNT-TC-1A certification. Kansas City is also home to large engineering, procurement and construction firms serving the power, water and utility sectors, which generates demand for Level III input on procedures and quality programmes.

Pipelines and terminals

Crude, natural gas and refined-product pipelines and storage terminals converge on the metro. Construction and integrity work uses RT and automated UT to API 1104, and terminals need tank and piping thickness surveys. Operator qualification under federal pipeline safety rules is a separate requirement handled by the operator.

Manufacturing and national security work

Automotive assembly plants on both sides of the state line, heavy equipment and agricultural manufacturers, and precision defence manufacturing all generate NDT demand, from weld and casting inspection to PT and UT on critical components. Aerospace suppliers in the region, including the Wichita aviation cluster, often require NAS 410 qualification; Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A-based and we are upfront about that.

Multi-state crews and why records matter

Because Kansas City contractors routinely send technicians across state lines and between very different clients, a clean certification file is a competitive asset. A rail customer, a utility and a pipeline operator may each audit the same technician's records in a single year, and each will check that training hours, experience, exam scores, vision tests and the Level III's signature are all present and consistent with the written practice. Employers who standardise their records early spend far less time on audits and can move technicians between jobs without delay. Our training records and Level III services are built to make that audit trail straightforward.

Bridges and infrastructure

The Missouri and Kansas rivers are crossed by numerous highway and rail bridges, and both state DOTs run major bridge programmes. Steel bridge fabrication and repair follow AWS D1.5, with UT and MT on critical welds.

Radiography licensing: Missouri versus Kansas

This is the most important local nuance for RT crews. Missouri is not an NRC Agreement State, so industrial radiography with radioactive material in Missouri is licensed and inspected directly by the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission under 10 CFR Part 34. Kansas is an Agreement State, so radiography there is licensed by the Kansas Department of Health and Environment's radiation control programme. A company working on both sides of State Line Road must hold the right licence, or file reciprocity, for each jurisdiction. Individual radiographers must meet radiation safety training, certification (for example ASNT's industrial radiography radiation safety programme or a recognised state certification), on-the-job training and dosimetry requirements. Atlantis RT courses teach the NDT method; the radiation safety component is separate and runs through your employer's licensed programme. Confirm current rules with the NRC and KDHE.

What Kansas City employers typically ask for

  • SNT-TC-1A Level II with a complete training, experience and exam record.
  • Multiple methods, especially UT plus MT/PT/VT for rail and fabrication work.
  • AWS D1.1/D1.5 knowledge for structural and bridge work; API 1104 for pipelines.
  • Travel flexibility across Missouri, Kansas and neighbouring states.
  • Some employers also ask for welding inspector or API inspector credentials; Atlantis does not train to those.

Level III services and written practices for Kansas City NDT companies

Fabricators, rail shops and smaller inspection contractors often need Level III capability without a full-time Level III on payroll. SNT-TC-1A allows an employer to designate an outside Level III. Atlantis provides:

  • Written practice development: see written practice development.
  • Procedures referencing AWS, ASME, API 1104 or customer specifications.
  • Examinations prepared and graded by a Level III.
  • Audit support for customer, EPC and quality-system audits.
  • Corporate training plans: see corporate NDT training.

Read SNT-TC-1A training and certification, then book a Level III consultation.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 NDT methods in five environments: NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site and storage tank. For Kansas City trainees, the welding workshop and oil and gas site scenarios match fabrication and pipeline work, and the storage tank scenario fits terminal inspection.

It is a practice tool only and does not replace hands-on training or the practical exam on real specimens.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees course content, examinations and employer certification support for Kansas City clients. Level III candidates can see ASNT Level III training.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Kansas City

How do I get NDT certified in Kansas City?

Your employer certifies you under SNT-TC-1A after you complete classroom training, documented experience, general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, and a vision test. Atlantis provides the training and outside Level III services.

Can I take NDT training online in Missouri or Kansas?

Yes. Theory and Level III preparation are available as live online classes. Practicals and the practical exam are completed onsite on real equipment and specimens. See online NDT training.

Is there an Atlantis NDT training centre in Kansas City?

No. Atlantis has no physical training centre in Kansas City; we deliver online and onsite at your facility.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your written practice. The recommended classroom and experience minimums are in our training requirements matrix; experience usually sets the timeline.

Do I need a license for radiography in Missouri?

Missouri is not an Agreement State, so radioactive-material radiography is licensed by the NRC. Your employer holds the licence; you must meet radiation safety training and certification requirements before working with sources.

Do I need a license for radiography in Kansas?

Kansas is an Agreement State, so KDHE licenses radiography. Companies crossing between Missouri and Kansas must have the correct licence or reciprocity for each state.

What does NDT training cost in Kansas City?

We quote on request, based on method, level, group size and delivery format. Request a Kansas City training quote; we reply within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Kansas City employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used framework across US fabrication, rail, pipeline and power work. Aerospace, nuclear and rail employers may add their own requirements on top.

Which method should I learn first for rail work?

MT and VT are common starting points, followed by UT for axles, wheels and rail welds. Your employer's programme decides the exact sequence.

Can you train our crew onsite?

Yes, anywhere in the Kansas City region, under ASNT Level III oversight. See corporate NDT training.

Does my company need a written practice?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A requires it before certifying anyone. See written practice development.

How do I prepare for the UT Level II exam?

Use UT Level 2 practice questions and the Practical NDT simulator alongside structured training.
